items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Dennis Wilson, who was playing trombone at the time, was playing some fine charts for the band too

ctx.x: Yeah, I must have been lousy that night. Because over the years I had my major drum solo was “Whirly Bird,” and then we pulled out “Summertime” which was an Eric Dixon arrangement as I recall. It was a very fine arrangement. And then Dennis Wilson, who was playing trombone at the time, was playing some fine charts for the band too and he wrote a thing called “Good Mileage” which was a big drum feature for me. But one night Basie called “Cute.” I don’t know where that came from but we played it one time. Another…
Four years to pull it out one time.
